rendering.assets: Authored procedural C meshes and embedded GLSL; no external models, textures or CDN dependencies
props: Branching broadleaf trees and conifers with roots, twigs and two-sided leaves
Irregular smooth boulders, pebbles and grass tufts
materials: GGX specular and roughness with filmic tone mapping
Wet shoreline tint and terrain-derived ambient occlusion
Cooled volcanic crust with emissive fissures

shadow_map.inspection: Disabled during assembly and active cutaway/isolation

water.cache: Refresh on camera, viewport aspect or assembly changes

rendering.webgl_compatibility: Retain rank texcoord input in every mesh shader and initialize the default batch normal attribute slot for Raylib 5.5 non-VAO fallback
rendering.regeneration: Paint busy state and disable controls before running synchronous generation/meshing outside the input event

browser_review.performance_scope: UI GetFPS samples in settled views; not a sustained benchmark. Brief frame-rate drops occur during rebuilds and camera/reflection updates. Mobile performance was not measured.
verified: Overview and close-up trees, rocks, terrain and shoreline
Frozen and volcanic palettes at floor 10
Camera rotation and cached reflection refresh
Auto cutaway, horizontal section and opaque terrain
Tunnel isolation with and without ceilings
Retained tile boundaries and unchanged map hashes
browser_review.console: Final packaged page had no error/warn console entries. Existing Raylib VAO/NPOT capability notices remain at log level. Temporary GL diagnostics were clean after the attribute fixes.

limitations: First realism pass, not a finished AAA asset pipeline.
Vegetation is static and cosmetic; it does not participate in collision.
The moving scout is not included in planar reflections.
The single shadow map loses detail at extreme zoom.
Ocean is a visual surface, not fluid simulation.
World meshing and GPU preparation still run synchronously and add several seconds beyond the reported core generation time.
